gloss: don't need; don't want; no thanks

definitions.explanation: The plain negative of {要|い}る (to need, to be required). Used colloquially to decline an offer or to say something is unnecessary.

examples.japanese: そんなにたくさんはいらない。
もう{古|ふる}いから、この{服|ふく}はいらないと{思|おも}う。
examples.english: It's already old, so I think I don't need this clothing anymore.

notes:
Plain negative of {要|い}る (to need). Functions as a short, casual refusal or rejection.

REGISTER:
Very casual. To family, friends, or in shops with close customers. In polite contexts, use いりません, {結構|けっこう}です, or {大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}です.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- 「(item)は?」「いらない。」: response declining an offer
- (item) はいらない: I don't need (item)
- もういらない: I don't need any more

SIMILAR WORDS:
- いりません: don't need (polite form)
- {結構|けっこう}です: no thank you — polite refusal of an offer
- {大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}です: I'm fine — soft, indirect refusal common in modern speech
